text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BAMERINDUS UNDER PRESSURE TO RESTRUCTURE

A sophisticated plan to restructure private bank Bamerindus and to sell off a controlling stake to national or international investors will go ahead once Senator Jose Eduardo de Andrade Vieira agrees to give up control of the bank.
-- GOVERNMENT DISCOVERS 1.5 BLN REAIS GAP
The Brazilian government has discovered an unexpected 1.5 billion reais ($1.5 billion) gap in treasury funds which could hamper some 42 projects planned by the government.
-- SALARIES ARE LEAVING INDEXATION BEHIND

Pay rises in many sectors of the economy are no longer being linked to inflation indices as previously. Many employees have reached agreements with their employers to improve their incomes through profit sharing or bonuses.
O GLOBO
-- MILITARY TO HELP IN FIGHT AGAINST DRUG TRAFFICKING
Brazil's first national security policy since the end of military dictatorship in the 1980s includes measures to involve the military in the fight against drug trafficking.
-- PRISON ESCAPE LANDS THREE PRISON GUARDS IN JAIL
Three prison guards have been arrested under suspicion of helping six prisoners escape from a jail in Rio de Janeiro.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- BRAZIL SUFFERS TOURISM DEFICIT OF $2.5 BLN

Brazilian tourists are spending more money abroad this year than foreign tourists are spending in Brazil, increasing the January to September deficit to $2.5 billion from $1.7 billion in the same period last year.
-- CAR EXPLODES AND KILLS SEVEN YOUNGSTERS IN CURITIBA
Seven people aged between 15 and 21 were killed when their car hit a truck and exploded on Saturday near the southern Brazilian city of Curitiba.
-- ADOPTIVE SON SUSPECTED OF KILLING PARENTS
Police say the adoptive son of an eldery couple who were found decapitated at their home in Marilia, Sao Paulo state, is a suspect in the case.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
